nodes.label: LLVM Broken Symlinks
nodes.rationale: When an LLVM build is inherited from another user, Python bindings under mlir_core contain broken symlinks pointing to the original builder's scratch path. Fixed by checking out clean source files and rewriting symlinks using rm + ln -s.

nodes.label: bf16 Lowering Crash
nodes.rationale: mlir-cpu-runner (LLVM JIT) cannot lower bf16 operations to executable x86 CPU code due to lack of hardware/lowering support, resulting in execution times of -1. Fixed by re-exporting the model in float32.

nodes.label: GPT2 JIT Causal Mask
nodes.rationale: HuggingFace's create_causal_mask is incompatible with PyTorch JIT tracing. Fixed by bypassing the HF forward path and manually implementing the causal + padding 4D mask in a pure-tensor wrapper (Model Surgery).

nodes.label: TiledFusion Constant Store Dimension
nodes.rationale: TiledFusion crashed when result store of a producer contained a constant literal dimension (e.g. '0'), since it was not in the loop variable mapping. Fixed by skipping constant dimensions that are not loop variables.

nodes.label: C++ Diagnostic Destructor Abort
nodes.rationale: C++ CollectDiagnosticsToStringScope asserts that error/warning messages are empty upon destructor execution. Warnings/remarks left in the scope abort the entire process. Fixed by isolating MLIR transformations in separate Python subprocesses.

nodes.label: MLIR Signal Handler Override
nodes.rationale: MLIR C++ context initialization overrides custom Python signal handlers. Fixed by explicitly re-registering the Python SIGABRT handler after MlirContext is initialized.

nodes.label: ONNX CPU Slowdown
nodes.rationale: ONNX Runtime is 29x slower than PyTorch eager on CPU due to lack of thread-binding optimization (affinity warnings) and lack of AVX-512 fused ops compared to PyTorch. PyTorch JIT was chosen over ONNX.

nodes.label: Out of Memory (OOM) Errors on Tensor Allocation
nodes.rationale: Synthetically generated or extracted MLIR benchmarks request multi-dimensional tensors that mandate RAM beyond Slurm memory limits, causing crashes. Fix includes pre-execution heuristic filtering (>8 GB size skip).
nodes.norm_label: out of memory (oom) errors on tensor allocation

nodes.label: Invalid MLIR Syntax Parse Failure
nodes.rationale: .mlir contains syntax that is malformed or incompatible with llvm-project 19.x branch. Fix is to prune dataset/quarantine.

nodes.label: C++ Binding Hard Crashes (SIGKILL)
nodes.rationale: Exit code -9. LLVM/MLIR Execution Engine inside C++ bindings segfaults or triggers OS OOM. Pre-filtering benchmarks helps.

nodes.label: Compilation/Execution Timeouts
nodes.rationale: JIT compilation or execution runs too long. Python signal.alarm() timeout of 15s prevents Slurm job hangs.

nodes.label: Batched In-Process MLIR Transform
nodes.rationale: Instead of calling action.apply() per action (which spawned a process to parse the model from scratch every time), compile one combined transform script and interpret it in-process. Reduced GPT-2 optimization time from 25h to 2-3 minutes.

nodes.label: Bufferization and Lowering Fallback Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Three-level execution pipeline: 1) bindings execution (300s cap); 2) multiprocess bindings (7200s); 3) mlir-opt subprocess + mlir-cpu-runner execution (7200s) to handle complex bufferization timeout/crashing patterns.

nodes.label: Dataset Stratification Pipeline
nodes.rationale: 80/20 stratified split with seed 42, representing 18 kept models and legacy pools proportionally in train/eval splits, outputting flat files.

nodes.label: Fake curl PATH Shadowing
nodes.rationale: Workaround for curl hanging on Slurm nodes: download install script manually, create a mock curl script, and run install script pre-pending the mock path to trigger fallback to wget.

nodes.label: Entropy Collapse
nodes.rationale: PPO policy becomes deterministic mid-training (entropy -> 0), freezing action selection. Caused by combination of Shaped Reward (strong consistent gradients) + Transformer (high representational capacity).

nodes.label: Full-Model RL Design
nodes.rationale: Addresses the limitation of scaling the per-op scheduling to end-to-end full-model scheduling by introducing global graph state, hierarchical action space, and full-model PPO training loops.

nodes.label: Abstraction Penalty
nodes.rationale: JVM JIT-compiles on cold starts and has memory/GC overhead, whereas LLVM compiles AOT once, allowing zero-cost abstractions, real-time safety, bare-metal capability, and MLIR hardware compilation.

nodes.label: Entropy Collapse
nodes.rationale: Shaped rewards in V4 cause policy to collapse to zero entropy as it exploits static estimators, preventing policy exploration. Hardcoding shaped rewards to zero resolves this.

nodes.label: Success-Contingent Reward Negation
nodes.rationale: Treatment of intermediate rewards as provisional, negating them if final compilation/execution crashes or slows down below baseline, removing gambler's incentive.

nodes.label: LLVM Build and Shared Fix
nodes.rationale: Cloning release/19.x with python bindings. Symlink recovery handles shared compilation where original paths were absolute paths of another user.

nodes.label: Hardware-Aware Features
nodes.rationale: Injecting cache sizes and SIMD width into observation vector enables generalization of compiler policies across CPU architectures.

nodes.label: Process-Isolated Execution
nodes.rationale: Running JIT execution in isolated multiprocessing child worker prevents compiler SIGABRTs and segment faults from killing main training loop.

nodes.label: Missing Loop Optimizations
nodes.rationale: Polyhedral loop optimizations like skewing, distribution, and peeling are currently excluded due to transform dialect maturity and safety analysis requirements.

nodes.label: Batch Complexity Policy
nodes.rationale: Groups benchmarks by size/operation complexity to prevent slow compilation steps from stalling parallel execution threads.

nodes.label: Lustre File Quota Safety
nodes.rationale: HPC Lustre soft/hard file counts constraints require manual monitoring and results database cleanup to prevent quota violations.

nodes.label: Paper Package Safety Upgrades
nodes.rationale: SIGABRT handler, subprocess isolation, dynamic timeout, and mlir-cpu-runner command fallback ported to paper packages to ensure unrecoverable MLIR native aborts do not crash evaluations.

nodes.label: Bergamo Pinning
nodes.rationale: Restricts all evaluations and training runs to bergamo CPU nodes to ensure performance measurements and timing results are consistent.

nodes.label: PyTorch Thread Capping
nodes.rationale: Capping PyTorch to 4 threads prevents context-switching overhead on lightweight networks, maximizing backpropagation compute efficiency.

nodes.label: Stratified Split Prefix Match Fix
nodes.rationale: Fixes prefix matching in model_family() to prevent bart, bert, and other compound models from dropping eval coverage.

nodes.label: Flat Results Directory Design
nodes.rationale: Simplifies directory structure and moves training markers to single cumulative JSON files to prevent inode bloat on HPC Lustre.

nodes.label: Novelty 1: Hardware-Aware Observation Space
nodes.rationale: The agent is blind to the hardware it optimizes for (a policy trained on a 4-core laptop is suboptimal on a 64-core server); injecting L1/L2/L3 cache sizes, physical vs logical cores, SIMD width (256 AVX2 / 512 AVX-512), and clock speed enables cross-hardware portability.

nodes.label: Novelty 2: Deep Loop Nest Parsing (Transformer Encoder)
nodes.rationale: LSTMs are sequential and struggle with long-range dependencies in nested loops; a transformer treats each loop level as a token so self-attention weighs outermost loop (tiling) against innermost loop (vectorization) simultaneously, with structural positional encoding for hierarchy.

nodes.label: Novelty 3: Multi-Objective and Shaped Rewards
nodes.rationale: Speedup is a sparse end-of-execution reward ignoring energy/memory; shape with static-analysis signals (arithmetic intensity, vectorization ratio) and weighted multi-objective R = w1(Speedup) + w2(PeakMemoryUsage). Lessons from V4.6/7/8: shaped reward must be <=10% of terminal reward (V4.5's dominated 20x, agent optimized static heuristics instead of runtime), anchor to log10(speedup) ±0.3-0.5 with reward_shaping_scale=0.05, zero intermediate rewards when speedup<1.0, vectorization bonus must scale with reward_shaping_scale (V4.5 added it after scaling — bug), use SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK not os.cpu_count(), MIN_EXEC_TIMEOUT 30s→2s with 10x→5x multiplier. Implemented in V4.5+.

nodes.rationale: Static 30s timeouts are unfair to large benchmarks: JIT compilation of tiled/fused MLIR makes the LLVM backend work harder, and '3x slower' is a richer PPO gradient than a binary 'Timed Out'. Baseline root_exec_time comes from V0 (unoptimized) results; cap at 300s.

nodes.label: Physical Boundary Safeguards (Vectorization depth limit 6)
nodes.rationale: A native C++ diagnostic-buffer-overflow bug in the MLIR Python bindings affects all versions; shaped rewards drove 'greedy exploration' into deep-nest crash zone (depth > 6) in V2/V4, so V4.5 and V2.5 mask Vectorization beyond depth 6 — defining physical boundaries, not cheating.

nodes.label: Defensive Reinforcement Learning
nodes.rationale: V4 had ~50% failure rate (native SIGABRTs in ResNet/ViT sequences, risk-incentive misalignment from partial shaped credit, strict 30s timeouts, greedy 5+ nested transforms). Defensive RL adds safeguards for near-zero failure rate without sacrificing integrated-model performance.

nodes.label: Success-Contingent Reward Negation
nodes.rationale: Eliminates the gambler's incentive: all intermediate shaped rewards are provisional and zeroed if final execution fails (timeout/crash/OOM); the policy must treat runnability as a hard constraint and gets only the final failure penalty (-20.0).
